@TiA4f8R 
Do we really need a database migration for this?
The users can simply delete their search history and the problems should be gone.
Looks a little bit overkill to me, also regarding the fact that it doesn't affect that many users.

Without the database migration, only a single class is affected, now we have 6...

> @TiA4f8R 
> Do we really need a database migration for this?

Disclaimer: the idea is not from me but from @TobiGr:

> the dev might want to add a migration finding duplicate entries in the search history and delete them, leaving just the trimmed one

@litetex I personally do not like to leave it up to the user to clean up the database to contain expected values.
It's better to know exactly how the data is structured. It's just the search history, but we should keep the db clean. I've learned that the hard way... (not in this project though)

I don't think it's a good idea to have the user manually clear the search history for this feature. Actually, NewPipe works fine with or without database migrations because the PR does not add a unique constraint to the ```search``` fields.

I don't know why SQL lets you do this, but you can't select one `id` from the `GROUP BY`, since there could be multiple `id`s in the same group, as you are not grouping by id. I would suggest to do `SELECT MIN(id)` for a more well-defined behavior, even though there would be no actual difference.

reply.body:
Should we handle other non-ASCII spaces? Like ```'\u3000'```. 
```String.trim()``` and ```org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.utils.Utils.isBlank()``` do not handle these code points. 
We should use ```String.strip()``` and ```String.isBlank()```, but they do not available in the current version of the Android SDK.
There is no need to, in my opinion

timeline.body:
Why trim it in the search field, too? Let the user type or paste what he wants and:
- trim the string before passing it to `suggestionPublisher`
- when the user presses search, set the trimmed string in the search bar, search for the trimmed string and save the trimmed string in the db

reply.body:
The above two behaviors have been implemented.

As trimming when pasting, it is inconsistent with the behavior of other search bars. I thought it's often unintentional for users to paste text with leading and trailing spaces. So I made this additional change.
